sentences.text:
Anil Kumar Bhardwaj vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 16 January,
2024
 1
 High Court Of Chhattisgarh, Bilaspur

Order Sheet
 Cra No. 672 of 2019
 Anil Kumar Bhardwaj S/o Tikedau Bhardwaj Aged About 26 Years R/o

Garhumariya, Police Chowki: Jootmil, Police Station Kotwali, District Raigarh
 Chhattisgarh.

---- Appellant
 Versus
 State Of Chhattisgarh Through Station House Officer, Police Chowki : Jootmil,
 Police Station Kotwali, District Raigarh Chhattisgarh.

---- Respondent
16/01/2024 Mr. Sanjay Agrawal, counsel for the applicant.
Mr. Priyanshu Gupta, Panel Lawyer for the State.
Heard on I.A. No. 07 of 2023 which is an application under Section 389 of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to applicant.

Applicant stands conviced and sentenced by the judgement of conviction and order of sentence dated 09.04.2019 passed in Session Trial No. 51 of 2018 by the learned Court of Incharge Additional Sessions Judge (FTC) Raigarh, (C.G.) with a direction to run all the sentences concurently in the following manner:-
 Conviction Sentence  U/s 450 of I.P.C. R.I. for 07 years & fine of Rs. 500/- & in default of payment of fine, additional S.I. for 15 days U/s 376 of I.P.C. R.I. for 07 years & fine of Rs.
500/- & in default of payment of fine, additional S.I. for 15 days.
U/s 506B of I.P.C. R.I. for 01 year & fine of Rs. 500/- & in default of payment of fine, additional S.I.
for 15 days.
U/s 323 of I.P.C. R.I. for 06 months & fine of Rs. 500/- & in default of payment of fine, additional S.I. for 15 days Learned counsel for applicant submits that this application is filed on the ground of delay in hearing of appeal and appellant underwent period of about 05 years & 06 months out of 07 years of jail sentence imposed upon him.

He further contended that appeal is likely to take some time for final hearing and in view of the decision of Hon. Supreme Court in case of Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another 2022 Volume 10 SCC Page 51 (para 64),
Anil Kumar Bhardwaj vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114833470/
1 sentence imposed on applicant be suspended and he be released on bail during pendency of this revision.

sentences.text: Learned State counsel opposing the submission made by learned counsel for applicant, would submit that in view of the evidence available against appellant, he may not be enlarged on bail and his sentence may not be suspended.
I have heard counsel for parties.

Perusal of impugned judgement would show that appellant was in jail from 16.05.2018 till 19.04.2019 (judgement of trial) and thereafter application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail, filed before this Court in criminal appeal, was dismissed as withdrawn and further he was granted temporary bail for a period of 10 days during pendency of appeal on 27.06.2019 till 09.07.2019.
In the aforementioned facts of the case, I am inclined to suspend the sentence imposed on applicant and to release him on bail during pendency of this appeal.
Accordingly, I.A. No. 07 of 2023 is allowed.

It is directed that substantive jail sentence imposed upon applicant shall remain suspended during pendency of this revision and he shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in sum of  25,000/- with one local surety in like sum to the satisfaction of concerned Trial Court, for his appearance bfore the Registry of this court on 14th of February, 2024.
Thereafter, he shall appear before the concerned Trial Court on the date to be given by the Registry of this Court and shall continue to appear there till final disposal of this revision.

Sd/-
